\section[a herança]{a herança — the inheritance}

\label{lesson:PT-C316-heranca}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the cemetery, then the Portuguese for the tomb.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a herança}
\textbf{a herança} — \textquotedblleft{}the inheritance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Com a herança, comprou uma casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{With the inheritance he bought a house.}
\end{quote}

Also what we receive from the past: \emph{a herança cultural}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{herança} comes down from Old Portuguese \emph{erança} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{haerentia} \textquotedblleft{}things that cling\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{haerēre} \textquotedblleft{}to cling\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a herança}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a herança}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a herança}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the cemetery, then the Portuguese for the tomb, then say \emph{a herança} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a herança mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The inheritance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[herdar]{herdar — to inherit}

\label{lesson:PT-C316-herdar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the tomb, then the Portuguese for the inheritance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: herdar}
\textbf{herdar} — \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Herdei os olhos azuis da minha mãe.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I inherited my blue eyes from my mother.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Herdar de alguém} — to inherit from someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{herdar} comes down from Old Portuguese \emph{erdar} (EtymDB), from Latin \emph{hērēditāre} \textquotedblleft{}to inherit\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{hērēs} \textquotedblleft{}an heir\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{herdar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{herdar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{herdar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the tomb, then the Portuguese for the inheritance, then say \emph{herdar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does herdar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To inherit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[o herdeiro]{o herdeiro — the heir}

\label{lesson:PT-C316-herdeiro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the inheritance, then the Portuguese for to inherit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o herdeiro}
\textbf{o herdeiro} — \textquotedblleft{}the heir\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O filho mais velho é o único herdeiro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The eldest son is the only heir.}
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{a herdeira}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{herdeiro} comes down from Old Portuguese \emph{erdeiro} (EtymDB) and goes back to Latin \emph{hērēditārius}, built on \emph{hērēs} \textquotedblleft{}an heir\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o testamento]{o testamento — the will, the testament}

\label{lesson:PT-C316-testamento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to inherit, then the Portuguese for the heir.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o testamento}
\textbf{o testamento} — \textquotedblleft{}the will, the testament\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O avô deixou um testamento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Grandfather left a will.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer testamento} — to make a will.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{testamento} comes from Latin \emph{testāmentum} \textquotedblleft{}a will\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{testārī} \textquotedblleft{}to bear witness\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a pensão]{a pensão — the pension; the guesthouse}

\label{lesson:PT-C316-pensao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the heir, then the Portuguese for the will.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a pensão}
\textbf{a pensão} — \textquotedblleft{}the pension; the guesthouse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A minha avó vive da pensão.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My grandmother lives on her pension.}
\end{quote}

Also a small, cheap guesthouse: \emph{ficámos numa pensão}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pensão} was borrowed from Latin \emph{pēnsiō} \textquotedblleft{}a payment, a rent\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{pendere} \textquotedblleft{}to weigh, to pay\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Revisão dos capítulos 309–316}

\label{lesson:PT-R316-revisao-309-316}



\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the birth, the delivery, pregnant, pregnancy, the newborn baby
  \item the christening, to baptise, the godfather, the godmother, to breastfeed
  \item childhood, adolescence, youth, old age, the generation
  \item the engagement, the wedding ring, the wedding, to propose, matrimony
  \item the honeymoon, the wedding anniversary celebration, the divorce, the separation, the move
  \item the passing, to pass away, the death, mourning, the wake
  \item the funeral, to bury, the burial, the cemetery, the tomb
  \item the inheritance, to inherit, the heir, the will, the pension
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The birth? (\textbf{o nascimento}.) The delivery? (\textbf{o parto}.) Pregnant? (\textbf{grávida}.) Pregnancy? (\textbf{a gravidez}.) The newborn baby? (\textbf{o recém-nascido}.) The christening? (\textbf{o batizado}.) To baptise? (\textbf{batizar}.) The godfather? (\textbf{o padrinho}.) The godmother? (\textbf{a madrinha}.) To breastfeed? (\textbf{amamentar}.) Childhood? (\textbf{a infância}.) Adolescence? (\textbf{a adolescência}.) Youth? (\textbf{a juventude}.) Old age? (\textbf{a velhice}.) The generation? (\textbf{a geração}.) The engagement? (\textbf{o noivado}.) The wedding ring? (\textbf{a aliança}.) The wedding? (\textbf{o casamento}.) To propose? (\textbf{pedir em casamento}.) Matrimony? (\textbf{o matrimónio}.) The honeymoon? (\textbf{a lua de mel}.) The wedding anniversary celebration? (\textbf{as bodas}.) The divorce? (\textbf{o divórcio}.) The separation? (\textbf{a separação}.) The move? (\textbf{a mudança}.) The passing? (\textbf{o falecimento}.) To pass away? (\textbf{falecer}.) The death? (\textbf{o óbito}.) Mourning? (\textbf{o luto}.) The wake? (\textbf{o velório}.) The funeral? (\textbf{o funeral}.) To bury? (\textbf{enterrar}.) The burial? (\textbf{o enterro}.) The cemetery? (\textbf{o cemitério}.) The tomb? (\textbf{o túmulo}.) The inheritance? (\textbf{a herança}.) To inherit? (\textbf{herdar}.) The heir? (\textbf{o herdeiro}.) The will? (\textbf{o testamento}.) The pension? (\textbf{a pensão}.)
